title: Cargo workspace dependency rules
description: Source of truth for which workspace crates may depend on which. docs/architecture/overview.md renders its crate graph from this file. The xtask architecture check (work package s0-workspace-skeleton) reads it, runs cargo metadata, and fails the build on any edge, kind or external dependency that this file does not allow. See ADR 0002.

rings.name: Domain
rings.rule: Pure model, state machines and contract types. No I/O, no clock, no randomness, no async runtime.

rings.name: Ports
rings.rule: Trait definitions the inner code needs from the outside. Depends on domain only. No I/O.

rings.name: Application and adapters
rings.rule: Application crates hold use cases and depend on domain and ports. Adapter crates implement ports and depend on domain and ports. Neither kind depends on the other, and no crate in this ring depends on a peer.

rings.name: Composition roots
rings.rule: Binaries. The only place where adapters are chosen and wired to use cases.

crates.name: domain
crates.responsibility: Identifiers, value objects, the Job, StageRun, Attempt and TaskNode state machines, guards, contract types that mirror schemas/, the ledger chain hash, policy evaluation (the 'policy crate' in docs/security is this module until its extraction trigger fires), secret redaction, assurance-level derivation.

crates.name: ports
crates.responsibility: Outbound traits and their closed error enums: Clock, IdGenerator, CancelSignal, Store with SystemTx and Tx and their parts, ArtifactStore, SandboxProvider, SandboxSession, WorkspaceProvider, Workspace, JobRepo, AgentRuntime, ModelRouter, ModelBroker, AgentRegistry, OutputValidator, SpecificationProvider, IssueSource, ChangeHost, WebhookVerifier and ProcessRunner. Also the pure checks that every adapter and fake must share: the sandbox spec validation and posture comparison, the path rules, and the protection preflight.

crates.name: workflow
crates.responsibility: The durable engine and all stage handlers: admission, scheduling, leases, retries, gate evaluation, rework routing, human decisions, plus the modules listed under deferred crates.

crates.name: spec_adapter
crates.responsibility: Anti-corruption layer for GitHub Spec Kit. Drives the four allowed skills, reads the produced files, and returns a SpecificationContract. The only crate that knows Spec Kit's file layout.

crates.name: storage

external_allow_notes.async-trait: Added by s1-xtask-extensions, which now enforces the allow list for adapters. storage implements port traits declared with #[async_trait], so it cannot implement them without the crate; ports and testkit already list it.
external_allow_notes.rustix: Added by s1-xtask-extensions. The local-filesystem ArtifactStore refuses a symbolic link at every step of a path with openat and no-follow flags. rustix is the safe binding (the workspace forbids unsafe code) and the only way to do that without a race between the check and the use. Features std and fs only.

crates.responsibility: PostgreSQL implementation of Store (Diesel, async), outbox writes, evidence ledger with hash chain, lease compare-and-swap, local-filesystem content-addressed ArtifactStore.

crates.name: runtime
crates.responsibility: AgentRuntime adapters for the Claude Code and Codex command line tools. Builds argument vectors from a closed allow list (bypass flags only for a verified sandbox target), probes capabilities, starts the tool inside the sandbox through SandboxSession, parses output, maps failures to a closed error set, and supports a later host tool bridge as a hardening option.

crates.name: sandbox
crates.responsibility: SandboxProvider and WorkspaceProvider over the Docker command line and host-side git. Three network profiles (fetch_deps, agent behind a per-job egress sidecar, verify with no network), the posture verifier that inspects a created container before it starts, the supervisor that enforces wall-clock and disk limits, redacted log streaming, the janitor, and the workspace side: mirror, sparse worktree, masked .git, host-side git with a fixed environment, the no-follow audit walk and the tree diff. The only crate that starts containers or runs git.

external_allow_notes.rustix: Added at integration of s1-sandbox-adapter. The ProcessRunner contract requires that a command that times out or is cancelled ends its whole process group, not only the direct child, so no stray process keeps running. Sending a signal to a process group has no safe route in the standard library, and the workspace forbids unsafe code, so the crate uses rustix with the std and process features only. The storage adapter already uses the same release (with fs). Decided by the lead, pending architect confirmation; if declined, GroupGuard falls back to a direct-child kill and the group postcondition of the contract is not met.

crates.name: github
crates.responsibility: IssueSource and ChangeHost against the GitHub REST API as a GitHub App: signs the App JWT, mints per-job, per-stage installation tokens narrowed to one repository, revokes them, verifies webhook signatures, deduplicates deliveries, checks the repository protection preflight, writes only sanitized text. Merging is not implemented.

external_allow_notes.ring: RS256 signing of the App JWT and the TLS crypto provider, so one crypto library does both jobs. Chosen in s1-github-adapter over rsa (RUSTSEC-2023-0071, an unfixed timing side channel that cargo deny rejects), over jsonwebtoken with aws-lc-rs (a second crypto stack) and over the openssl command line (DEP-10 allows only docker and git to be started). Signing sits behind the JwtSigner trait so a signing service can replace it. cargo deny and cargo audit pass with the unchanged deny.toml. A new direct dependency needs a human decision: applied by the lead at integration, pending confirmation by the project owner.
external_allow_notes.ureq: Blocking HTTP client with rustls only, behind the transport trait, so tests use plain HTTP over loopback to the fake GitHub server and production uses TLS. Same decision record as ring.
external_allow_notes.async-trait: The adapter implements port traits that are declared with async_trait, as the storage adapter does.

crates.name: contracts

external_allow_notes.saphyr-parser: Added by s1-xtask-extensions. It replaces the free-text entry for a maintained YAML parser: work package s0-contracts-and-registry chose it (pure safe Rust, YAML 1.2) and the evidence is in the crate documentation, module yaml.
external_allow_notes.regex: Added by s1-xtask-extensions. The regular expression dialect the policy file names, for the schema pattern keyword and to check that every policy regex compiles. Features std and unicode-perl only.
external_allow_notes.globset: Added by s1-xtask-extensions. The glob dialect the policy file names, used only to check that every glob compiles.
external_allow_notes.serde_jcs: Added by s1-xtask-extensions. RFC 8785 canonical JSON, the input to the policy hash; the same crate domain uses for the ledger chain.

crates.responsibility: Embeds schemas/, implements OutputValidator, loads and validates agent manifests, domain capability profiles and policy files.

crates.name: egress
crates.responsibility: The model broker and the egress relay. The broker holds the real provider keys, issues and revokes per-job tokens, forwards only allowed API paths, and meters usage against the job ceiling. The relay is the per-job sidecar: exact-host allowlist, rejection of private and metadata address ranges after resolution, pinned connections and a byte quota. Implements ModelBroker.

external_allow_notes.ring: Digest of the token hash and of the bodies (sha2 is avoided so one crypto library serves the crate), and the TLS crypto provider of the upstream client. Same decision record as the GitHub adapter; cargo deny and cargo audit pass. Applied by the lead at integration, pending confirmation by the project owner.
external_allow_notes.httparse: Parses the HTTP/1 request head on the broker listener, with strict limits. Small, widely used, no unsafe code of ours.
external_allow_notes.ureq: Blocking HTTP client with rustls only, for the upstream call to the model provider, with redirects and proxies off. Same decision record as the GitHub adapter.

crates.name: observability
crates.responsibility: Initializes tracing and OpenTelemetry for the binaries and owns span and attribute naming.

crates.name: testkit
crates.responsibility: Labelled fakes: FakeClock, InMemoryStore, FakeSandbox, FakeAgentRuntime, FakeModelBroker, FakeChangeHost, FakeWorkspaceProvider, FakeJobRepo, FakeSpecificationProvider, ScriptedProcessRunner and FakeWebhookVerifier, with FakeRemote shared by the workspace and change host fakes. Every fake reports fidelity fake. Also the shared contract suites and the register that shows every check can fail. May appear only in dev-dependencies.

apps.name: api
apps.responsibility: HTTP API: GitHub webhook endpoint with signature verification, job submission, decisions, status and timeline queries, health endpoints.

apps.name: worker
apps.responsibility: Runs the engine loop in one process: claim, execute stage handlers, sweep leases and deadlines, supervise sandboxes, and host the model broker listener in Slice 1. Single concurrency in Slice 1.

apps.name: cli
apps.responsibility: Operator command line: submit, status, timeline, approve, reject, rework, pause, resume, cancel, probe. Calls the same use cases in process in Slice 1.

apps.name: egress-sidecar
apps.responsibility: The per-job relay binary, shipped as a container image next to the sandbox image. Holds no real credential.

tooling.name: xtask
tooling.responsibility: Cargo xtask binary that runs the architecture checks. Not part of the product. May use std and serde_json only.

rules.statement: A library crate depends only on workspace crates listed in its depends_on. Any other workspace edge fails the build.
No crate depends on a crate in the same or a higher ring, except that ports depends on domain.

rules.enforced_by: xtask check-architecture, from the dependency kind in cargo metadata

rules.statement: Rings 0 and 1 and the application crates use only the external crates in external_allow. Adding one needs an architect-reviewed change to this file.
domain, ports, workflow and spec_adapter contain no call to the clock, the filesystem, the network or process spawning. The clock comes from the Clock port.
rules.enforced_by: clippy disallowed-methods and disallowed-types in each crate's clippy.toml, verified with cargo clippy -D warnings

rules.statement: Third-party licenses and advisories pass policy.
Binaries are the only crates that depend on more than one adapter.

Store::begin_system is called only from the workflow crate, and ChangeHost has no method whose name starts with merge. The sources of the Spec Kit layout (.specify, speckit) appear only in spec_adapter, its fixtures and documentation.
Only the sandbox crate spawns docker or git. Only the runtime crate spawns an agent command line tool. No crate spawns a shell. The set of allowed spawned binaries is docker and git.
rules.enforced_by: xtask check-architecture by source scan, plus the process spawn recorder in the end-to-end tests (negative test ST-03 and FX-SPAWN)

source_scans.description: The lists that the source scans of xtask check-architecture use. They were constants in the xtask sources; a reviewer now changes them here. Every crate named below must be in crates or apps, or the check stops. Crate names are the names in this file, without the package prefix.

generated_artifacts.name: the schema and example index of the domain tests
the ledger chain fixture, against the independent Python oracle

resolved_features.reason: ADR 0011: the inner crates read the time from the Clock port. The std feature of time provides OffsetDateTime::now_utc, and Cargo unifies features across the workspace. The diesel crate, which the storage adapter needs, depends on time with its default features (std, macros), so those resolve for domain and ports as well and cannot be removed while diesel is in the workspace graph. The guard is therefore the clippy ban on time::OffsetDateTime::now_utc and now_local in every inner crate, which this same rule requires and which a test proves fires. A new feature such as local-offset (it provides now_local) still fails here. Decided at integration, pending architect confirmation. The resolved feature set is read from cargo metadata, not from the domain manifest.
ADR 0002: identifiers come from the IdGenerator port. The v1, v3, v4, v5, v6, v7 and v8 features and rng/fast-rng provide generators, so none of them may resolve for the inner crates.

workflow lists tokio[sync,time,rt,macros]. net, process, io-util and rt-multi-thread resolve because adapters and dev-dependencies enable them, and Cargo unifies them into the one tokio that workflow sees; the DEP-05 bans on tokio::net, tokio::process and tokio::fs paths are what stops workflow from using them. signal is enabled by apps/worker so that SIGTERM and SIGINT drain the loop instead of abandoning a lease; it adds no crate to Cargo.lock and workflow has no path to it. A new feature (fs, full) appearing in this set needs an architect-reviewed change here.

deferred.name: repository_intel
deferred.extract_when: A syntax-tree or symbol-graph index brings heavy parser dependencies, or a second consumer outside workflow needs it.
deferred.why_deferred: Slice 1 needs language detection, build and test command discovery, CODEOWNERS, protected paths and an ADR and docs inventory. That is a few hundred lines over the bounded repository reader, with no heavy dependency.

deferred.name: planner
deferred.extract_when: Incremental replanning, the critic loop and the Team Composer arrive, or the DAG validator gains a second consumer.
deferred.why_deferred: Slice 1 has one planner call and one pure DAG validator. Both depend on the same ports as every other stage handler.

deferred.name: quality
deferred.extract_when: The gate catalog needs tool-specific dependencies (static analysis, mutation, fuzzing) or domain-pack gates.
deferred.why_deferred: Slice 1 gates are commands run in the sandbox from trusted definitions plus pure evaluators of their reports.

deferred.name: documentation
deferred.extract_when: Domain documentation packs and the documentation DAG are built.
deferred.why_deferred: The stage exists as first-class stage kinds in the state machine from Slice 1. Its code does not need its own crate yet.

deferred.name: policy
deferred.interim_home: module domain::policy for pure evaluation, loaders in contracts
deferred.extract_when: The policy language needs its own parser or engine, or a consumer outside workflow appears.
deferred.why_deferred: Policy evaluation is a pure function of typed facts. The YAML files are owned elsewhere and loaded by contracts.

deferred.name: events
deferred.interim_home: outbox rows written by storage in Slice 1; no relay
deferred.extract_when: Slice 2 adds the outbox relay to NATS JetStream and idempotent consumers.
deferred.why_deferred: Slice 1 has no event consumer. The outbox table is written from day one so nothing needs retrofitting.

deferred.name: evals
deferred.why_deferred: Nothing to evaluate before a real end-to-end run exists.

deferred.name: domain_registry, capabilities, team_composer, toolchain_registry, research, experiment_tracking, artifact_catalog, validation_profiles, worker_capabilities
deferred.extract_when: Dynamic team composition and open-world domain discovery are implemented.
deferred.why_deferred: Slice 1 resolves one static profile (general-software). The schemas exist so the registries can be added without changing orchestration code.

deferred.name: apps/dashboard
deferred.why_deferred: Not part of the end-to-end proof.

deferred.name: apps/scheduler
deferred.extract_when: Slice 2 separates scheduling from execution and adds multiple workers. The model broker listener may move to its own binary at the same time.
deferred.why_deferred: One process is enough to prove the end-to-end path. Leases and fencing are built in Slice 1 so the split is a deployment change.
